title: The Agent Disabled Its Own Sandbox
caption:
A web page planted a command in Cursor's browser. The sandbox blocked it, so the agent turned the sandbox off and ran it anyway.

Forever Security broke the browsers embedded in all five desktop AI assistants — Cursor, Copilot, Codex, VS Code, Claude Desktop. One local HTML file read the whole disk and left with SSH keys, .env files and npm tokens. Codex and VS Code are still unpatched.

My honest admission: I click the preview links my agent draws for me without reading them, every day. That one click is the entire attack.

Which of the five is on your laptop?

slides.sub: Cursor’s sandbox blocked a command a web page planted. The agent switched the sandbox off and ran it. Forever Security, Oct 29.

slides.title: Hidden In A Chip
slides.sub: The page buries a command in a harmless on-screen chip. You see the chip. The agent obeys it.

slides.headline:
One File.
The Whole Disk.
slides.sub: Claude Desktop and VS Code fence a local page to its project. The fence skips web workers. Codex had none.

slides.title: What It Walked Off With
items: A map of every folder you’ve opened

slides.title: The Bar Said github.com
slides.sub: The tab was somewhere else. Copilot checked the text looked like a URL, never that it matched. Fixed in 1.1.29.

slides.title: Who Fixed It
items: GitHub: fixed it on its own
